images.filename: The Opening in to the Narrow Path above the Siri Bolan.jpg
images.caption: The Opening in to the Narrow Path above the Siri Bolan from James Atkinson's Sketches in Afghaunistan; published by H Graves & Co, London in 1839. Containing lithographic copies in 1842 of Atkinson's originals by Charles and Louis Hague. The publication is a folio of 25 tinted lithographed plates showing the topography and landscapes of Afghanistan and the Punjab creating an important record of what was then an unexplored country. James Atkinson was Superintending Surgeon of the Army of the Indus during the First Afghan War.
images.alt: The Opening in to the Narrow Path above the Siri Bolan from James Atkinson's Sketches in Afghaunistan; published by H Graves & Co, London in 1839. Containing lithographic copies in 1842 of Atkinson's originals by Charles and Louis Hague. The publication is a folio of 25 tinted lithographed plates showing the topography and landscapes of Afghanistan and the Punjab creating an important record of what was then an unexplored country. images.caption:
View from Michni Post at Khyber Pass near Torkham border crossing.
The picture depicts the tunnels of the Khyber Pass Railway (abandoned section Landi Kotal–Torra Tigga) in the Khyber Agency near Torkham, the area which is the border and main trade route between Pakistan and Afghanistan. The road is the Khyber Pass (part of the N-5, and Grand Trunk Road) that joins Peshawar, Pakistan, with Kabul, Afghanistan. One of the most historical passes of the world as Alexander the Great entered the subcontinent through this route.
